These structures, with their leaning facades and faded yellow brick walls, blend seamlessly with the rustic charm of the stacked sedge and tarpaulin mats that adorn the storefronts, creating a visually striking tableau. A defining feature of Hang Chieu Street is the moss-covered gray brick arch gate of Ô Quan Chưởng, which stands majestically at the end of the street, serving as a silent sentinel over the passage of time.

As night falls, the street transforms into a lively scene, where vendors set up stalls on the sidewalks, offering a range of culinary delights such as steaming bowls of mì vằn thắn and warm chè sắn, attracting a steady stream of visitors seeking late-night snacks. The cultural significance of Hang Chieu Street extends beyond its commercial activities, embodying the timeless spirit of the Old Quarter.
